<details>
<summary>📁 The Story So Far</summary>

**Campaign position:** Session 3 of 5. Regional stakes (Session 2: Germanic raid, Tribune's agenda, fort in chaos) escalate to divine. The party retrieved a cursed weapon, survived a siege, made enemies of Rome's administration, and is now carrying the problem into enemy territory on foot.

**What happened last session:**

- Tribune Lucius arrived with Senate authority and demanded the spear
- The Germanic raid hit the fort the same night — suspicious timing confirmed
- Vercingetorix the Red either became an ally or an enemy
- Quintus Flavius (Sextus' killer) departed unseen inside the Tribune's entourage or was exposed
- The party left the fort as fugitives, allies, or under ambiguous orders — depending on what they chose

**What players currently believe:**

- The grove is the only place the spear can be destroyed
- They have two days of travel through hostile territory
- Thusnelda may or may not be trustworthy
- The Legate is probably following

**What they don't know yet:**

- One party member is already under the spear's influence
- Thusnelda knew they were coming (she performed augury three days ago)
- Senator Brutus has launched the fort's siege specifically because they left
- The grove demands something permanent — not a token

**Open threads coming in:**

- What did the spear do to the person who carried it longest?
- Can Cassia's divine heritage help or is it another vulnerability?
- Is Vercingetorix's alliance solid or conditional?

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 The Truth Behind the Session</summary>

**What is actually going on:**

The spear is not passive cargo. It has been slowly extending a thread of influence into whoever in the party had the highest corruption or the most contact with it in Session 1. That person has been sleepwalking toward the spear at night, dreaming about it, and unconsciously advocating for keeping it. They don't know they're doing it. The spear does not want to be destroyed.

The grove is real, ancient, and demands something real. Thusnelda has run this ritual once before — fifty years ago, with Vercingetorix's grandfather. That party failed because one member offered something they could afford to lose. The grove knew. Nothing happened.

Senator Brutus launched the fort's siege when his intelligence network reported the party was heading into the forest with the spear. He does not know about the grove. He launched the siege to destabilize Vindolanda before they return, to make "returning home" impossible. He is acting on incomplete information.

**NPC schedules — what happens if players do nothing:**

- Thusnelda: Waits at the outer perimeter, then leads them through. She will complete the ritual alone if the party is incapacitated — she will succeed, but she will never speak to anyone about it.
- Legate Corvinus: Closes the gap by 4–6 hours per day. Arrives at the river crossing at the worst possible moment.
- Mars: Off-screen through Scenes 1–4. Present in Scene 5 regardless of what the party does.
- Senator Brutus: Off-screen all session. The siege of Vindolanda begins on Day 2 of travel.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 0: Cold Open</summary>

**Start in media res — the camp is wrong.**

Five seconds of silence before you speak. Then:

> *You wake before dawn. The forest is completely silent.*
>
> *Not quiet. Silent. No birds. No insects. No wind in the branches. The kind of silence that has weight.*
>
> *The spear is glowing.*
>
> *A faint red light pulses from its wrappings like a heartbeat. Around the cart — everything within five feet of it is still. A leaf is frozen mid-fall between the spear and the ground.*
>
> *One of your companions is standing beside it. They've been there for some time. They aren't moving.*
>
> *On a nearby tree, carved deep into the bark:*
>
> **MARS VIDET OMNIA**

**Hand out Handout 7 now.** Do not explain who carved it. Do not resolve the companion's sleepwalking. Cut to Scene 1 immediately.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 1: Something is Wrong</summary>

**The three clues to the influenced NPC — give these out over Scenes 1–3:**

| Clue | Check | What they find |
|---|---|---|
| Physical signs | Perception DC 13 (passive during travel) or Medicine DC 13 (active exam) | Eyes faintly red in direct light; rubbing the same spot on their arm; sleeps facing the spear even when it moved |
| Behaviour | Insight DC 14 (active: watching them during any spear conversation) | Advocates keeping the spear, can't articulate why; visibly agitated if others touch it; micro-pause before "I'm fine" |
| Spear reaction | Arcana DC 13 (passive) or Religion DC 14 (passive: examining the wrappings) | The spear physically tilts toward that person; Cassia sees the thread immediately if she looks |

**Pass the private note to the influenced player at session start:**
*"You woke last night and stood beside the spear for two hours. You don't remember doing it. The spear feels warm when you're near it. It has been making an argument, quietly, that makes a certain kind of sense: the power in this weapon could protect the people you care about. You haven't told anyone. You're not sure you're wrong."*

**d10 travel events** — roll once per 4-hour march or choose by feel:

| d10 | Event |
|---|---|
| 1 | Spear angles north on flat ground. DC 12 Arcana/Religion: tracking toward the grove instinctively |
| 2 | Lone Roman scout on a ridge. Follow, warn, or ignore — he'll report either way |
| 3 | Germanic watchers in the treeline. Vercingetorix can end it. Without him: Persuasion DC 14 with any Germanic phrase |
| 4 | The influenced character wakes screaming mid-march: vision of themselves standing over the party's bodies, holding the spear, smiling |
| 5 | Germanic offering-post at a path fork. Leave it alone. Disturbing it: wildlife avoids camp (Legate's trackers gain advantage) |
| 6 | Old Bones: a shallow valley, ground wrong underfoot. Investigation DC 12: a corroded pilum head, a belt buckle, bone -- a Roman column died here generations ago. This is Varro's family history (his shame is six generations of Teutoburg, in this exact forest); if any character knows that, it lands harder. Varro is not present to react to it himself. |
| 7 | Spear goes quiet for hours, then resumes stronger. Corruption 2+: DC 11 Wisdom save or urge to unwrap it "just to check" |
| 8 | Cold rain. Movement halved. Legate's trackers unaffected. No cloak = 1 level exhaustion without 2 hours shelter |
| 9 | Abandoned camp, fire ash still warm. Investigation DC 11: three people fled south-southeast; one was dragged. Drag marks end 40 ft from fire at soft dark earth. One item left: sealed pouch, 6 days hardtack, a Brigantes bronze ring |
| 10 | Boundary stone, knee-high granite, older than Rome. Religion DC 12: threshold between living world and Vættir land. Thusnelda leaves hair wound around a pebble at its base without explaining |

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 1b: The Boundary Stone — Riddle</summary>

**Run this as a dedicated scene — not a d10 roll.** Place it on Day 2 of travel, one hour before the Farbog. Travel event 10 is the trigger; give it the full treatment below.

**Read aloud:**

> *The path narrows between two moss-covered oaks. At the gap's center, a granite slab rises knee-high from the earth — older than any Roman stonework in this region. The carvings on it spiral inward, holding traces of ochre and red pigment.*
>
> *Thusnelda stops. She does not step forward.*
>
> *"The old ones ask a question before they let you pass," she says quietly. "I will translate. The answer must come from you. I will not give it."*

She reads the stone for a moment, then speaks:

> *"I travel between enemies without walking. I am forged in darkness and tested in flame. Armies fail without me. Gods demand me. I take years to build and a heartbeat to destroy. Without me, the ritual at the grove will not hold."*

**Answering the riddle:**

| Answer | Response |
|---|---|
| Trust / *fides* / loyalty | Accepted. Stone glows faintly gold. Easier Farbog navigation: Perception DC 9 instead of DC 11. |
| Courage / *virtus* / honor | Also accepted. Thusnelda: *"The old tongue has one word for all of these."* Same effect. |
| The spear / power / strength | Thusnelda: *"You are thinking like soldiers. Think like the land."* One more attempt allowed. |
| Wrong on second attempt | Stone dims. A cold shadow detaches from its base: one automatic Disrespect trigger in the Farbog. |
| Any thematically valid answer | DM's call. Peace, patience, faith — all work. The stone rewards intent. |

**Religion DC 12 (passive):** The carvings mark the threshold between the living world and Vættir land. The stone is not a monument. It is a gate. The question is the toll.

Thusnelda will not re-read or interpret the riddle after she has spoken it. "The stone heard. We can discuss it after we have crossed."

**Why it matters:** The party's answer shapes Thusnelda's language at the grove ritual. If they answered with trust: she frames the required sacrifice as an act of faith. If courage: she frames it as a test of worth. She will use their own words back at them, quietly, at the worst possible moment.

::: {.dm-note}
**If debate runs more than 5 real-world minutes:** *"The stone has no patience."* She waits. She does not cross. This is not a threat — but it is felt as one.

**If no one has Religion proficiency:** The stone is still translatable by Thusnelda regardless. The Religion DC only reveals the gate nature of the stone — additional context, not required to proceed.

**If the party ignores the stone and walks past:** The shadow follows anyway. They insulted the gate without answering. Two Disrespect triggers for the Farbog — guaranteed Vættir encounter.
:::

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 2: Thusnelda's Scouts</summary>

**If allied with Vercingetorix:** Four forest-dark figures appear. He raises a fist. They stop. The scouts lead the party to Thusnelda. *Toll: information about Roman troop movements. Technical treason. Practically necessary.*

**If not allied:** Ambush — 12 Tribal Warriors + 2 Scouts (CR 1/2). Perception DC 12 before initiative: semi-circle of disturbance to both flanks, none ahead. Ends diplomatically on Persuasion DC 14 with any Germanic phrase, or by demonstrating they want to destroy the spear. Vercingetorix arrives regardless after 3+ rounds.

**Thusnelda — first impression:**

A small, ancient-looking Germanic woman. Oak staff carved with spiraling runes. She smells of pine smoke and something metallic. She looks at the spear, then at the party, with the calm gaze of someone who has spent decades looking at hard things.

> *"God-Killer. Still breathing. I had hoped you would destroy it by now. I see you have not."*

**Hand out Handout 6 here** on DC 14 Persuasion success or Vercingetorix's vouching.

**Thusnelda's key lines:**

- On how she knows: *"My teacher's teacher sealed it. I have been waiting since I was eleven years old. I am seventy-three. You are late."*
- On alternatives: *"There is not another way. I have thought about this for sixty years. The grove is the only place. This is not an opinion."*
- On the influenced NPC: *"Your friend there has a thread in them. Cut it soon. The forest is not kind to loose threads."*
- On the sacrifice: *"Fear the grove's demand. Most people who come here choose something that hurts a little. That is not enough. The grove will know."*

**What she will and will not say:**

| She will say | She will not say |
|---|---|
| Exactly what the ritual requires | What the "right" sacrifice is for any specific character |
| That the grove rejects insufficient sacrifices | Whether a sacrifice is "good enough" before it is offered |
| That someone in the party is influenced | Who — she knows, but it is the party's work to discover |

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 3: The River Crossing</summary>

**The river:** 90 feet wide. Fast-moving. Three options:

| Method | Check | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Swim across | Athletics DC 13 (active) | Full gear counts as difficult terrain |
| Cross the fallen oak | Acrobatics DC 11 (active) | Knocked off: DC 13 Athletics or swept 20 ft downstream |
| String a rope | Athletics DC 10 (active, group) | All subsequent crossings have advantage |

**A small escort catches up exactly mid-crossing — not the full weight of the cohort:**
- 3 Legionaries (Guard stat blocks)
- 1 Centurion (Knight stat block, CR 3)
- Corvinus himself is never here. He is "one day behind" all session, deliberately -- he wants the spear destroyed and cannot be seen letting it happen.

**The split-party set piece:** Half on the far bank, half crossing. Ranged combat across the water (half cover). Melee on the fallen log. This should resolve in a round or two against a handful of unmotivated men -- not a war.

**Moral weight:** These soldiers are following soft orders ("prevent the crossing," not "kill them"). They don't want this fight either.

| Option | Check | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Order them to stand down | Intimidation DC 14 (active, centurion-rank character) | Centurion hesitates, long enough to cross and deny the ford. 5 above: he signals hold. |
| Claim mission is sanctioned | Deception DC 15 (needs tangible document or seal) | Without evidence: DC 18. With it: centurion wavers. |
| Destroy the log | No check | Severs pursuit. Anyone still on the near bank is cut off. |
| Let them cross | — | Full fight, but a short one -- these four men are here to be seen trying, not to die for it. |

*Varro does not travel with the party this session (see the Prologue) -- he is not present at the river. If the fight happens anyway, the Centurion calls it off after the first solid hit: "Enough. Let them go. I did not sign on to die for a Senator's argument with the gods."*

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 3b: The Farbog</summary>

**Read aloud when the ground turns soft:**

> *The grass shortens, then disappears. Water appears between the roots. The trees grow thin and angular, their trunks bone-pale, dead branches reaching sideways rather than up.*
>
> *The smell is iron and rot and something sweet underneath. Not pleasant-sweet. The smell of things left here a long time.*
>
> *Thusnelda raises one hand. "There are old ones here. Do not touch the water. Do not take anything. Do not run. If something approaches — stop and let me speak first."*
>
> *Far ahead, deeper in, a light pulses once. Blue-white. Then dark.*

**Run one, two, or all three below. Each takes 10–15 minutes.**

**Disrespect tracker:** Mentally count transgressions (disturbing offerings, attacking the Myling, taking from the sacrifice site, ignoring the boundary stone). Two or more triggers Encounter C.

**Encounter A — The Myling:**

Child-shaped, translucent, wrong. Standing on a hummock 30 feet off the path. Hands out. Does not approach.

- Ignore it: follows at 20 feet, weeps after 10 minutes. DC 13 Wisdom save or Frightened 1 hour. One disrespect.
- Acknowledge it (Religion DC 12, active): *"Unnamed one, we see you"* + drop any item of value into the water. It nods. Stills. Thusnelda exhales.
- Attack it: it dissipates. Two more appear at the next hummock.
- Ask Thusnelda: she knows the rite but it costs her — one ritual prep action in Scene 4 takes an extra round.

*If Cassia is present and the party performs the rite: she watches the spirit still. "The Romans burn our dead. The Germans bury theirs. We both know the same thing — that the dead need witness." Let it breathe.*

**Encounter B — The Bog Sacrifice Site:**

Twenty meters off the path: offering pole, three meters tall, knotwork carvings. At its base, offerings in birch bark. Beneath the water: a preserved human figure.

- Investigation DC 13 (active): site maintained recently. New bark wrappings. A Roman military sandal buckle.
- Religion DC 15 (active, one minute contact with pole): two religious traditions active. One old, rooted. One new, hot, angry. Not in harmony.
- Thusnelda: *"Someone has been using our holy sites. For something else. Mars has been here."*
- Cassia's herb quest: bog valerian blooms along the far bank. Nature DC 13 to identify. Gathering requires leaving the path. Perception DC 11 to spot the soft ground first. Payoff in Session 4: Siege Ward (3 uses, 2d8 HP + 1 exhaustion level each).

**Encounter C — Hostile Vættir (conditional: two+ disrespect triggers):**

Five, seven, more blue-white lights move toward the path. Purposefully.

Use Will-o'-Wisp stat blocks (CR 2): cannot flee, cannot be Turned, deal cold damage.

Dispersed by Group Acknowledgment: every party member simultaneously drops one item of value into the water channels. DC 10 Religion (group, one action each) to coordinate.

- Success: lights halt, pause, drift back one by one.
- Failure: one additional Vættir per round. Cannot be outrun. Thusnelda performs the rite alone if party falls — she succeeds but arrives at the grove visibly exhausted and answers in shorter sentences for the rest of the session.

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 3c: The Watching Post — Rune Lock (Puzzle)</summary>

**Location:** Fifty metres off the main path, visible from the rise before the bog proper. Run after Encounter A (Myling) and Encounter B (Sacrifice Site), before reaching the standing stones.

**Read aloud:**

> *Four standing stones form a small roofless chamber. The floor is packed earth with a circular depression at its centre — an old fire pit. The ash inside is recent. Someone has been here within the week.*
>
> *On the north stone, a fitted plug seals a natural cavity. Set into the plug's face in a ring: five flat rune tiles, each carved from a different type of stone. One socket is slightly recessed, a finger's width deeper than the rest. The others sit flush, waiting.*

**The five tiles:**

| Rune | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ᛗ | MANNAZ | Man / Humanity |
| ᚱ | RAIDHO | Journey / Ride |
| ᚹ | WUNJO | Joy / Pleasure |
| ᚦ | THURISAZ | Danger / Giant / Thorn — **decoy** |
| ᛖ | EHWAZ | Horse / Movement — **decoy** |

**Correct sequence:** ᛗ → ᚱ → ᚹ (MANNAZ, then RAIDHO, then WUNJO.)

**The clue:** Thusnelda's Map (Handout 6) has three small runes written in the bottom margin: *ᛗ ᚱ ᚹ* with the inscription *mannaz raidho wunjo* — "The man who makes this journey finds what he seeks."

| Check | DC | What they learn |
|---|---|---|
| Arcana (active: comparing tiles to the map) | 12 | "Three of these tiles match the runes on the map. The map's order is the sequence." |
| Religion (active: same comparison) | 11 | Same result. The runes form a ritual sentence — a statement of intent. |
| Trial and error (no check) | — | Works. Each wrong sequence triggers the warding seal before tiles reset. |

**Warding seal (wrong sequence):** 1d6 cold damage to whoever is touching the lock. Tiles reset. Pressing THURISAZ or EHWAZ as first or second: seal triggers immediately — they are decoys placed to punish impatience.

**Contents on success:**
- Sealed clay flask: *oil of slipperiness* (1 dose) — immediately useful for bog mud (Athletics DC 13 becomes DC 9)
- Folded leather strip: crude map confirming the grove's exact location
- Wax tablet: *IF YOU ARE READING THIS, YOU ARE LOOKING FOR THE SAME THING WE WERE. WE FAILED. DO NOT STOP.*

**If Thusnelda sees the tablet:** *"They got further than I thought. I did not know they reached the ruins."* She does not elaborate. Her expression does.

::: {.dm-note}
The tablet was left by Vercingetorix's grandfather's warband — the party that failed the ritual fifty years ago, the failure Thusnelda has carried since she was twenty-three. She will not share this unless the party earns that trust at the grove.

The puzzle rewards players who kept Handout 6 and actually read it. Do not hint at the handout connection unless the party has been stuck for 10+ real-world minutes — the moment of recognition is the payoff.

If someone presses THURISAZ first: appropriate, honestly. The rune means danger. The seal knows.
:::

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 4: The Sacred Grove</summary>

**Approaching the grove:**

Survival DC 11 (active: reading the ground before stepping into the stone ring): the grass is absent in a perfect circle, not grazed. Two natural cover positions: behind the north stone and behind the south stone. Useful in Scene 5 — each displaces an animated golem's movement by one full round.

**Read aloud:**

> *Seven standing stones ring a granite altar. Each stone is twice your height, carved with spiraling runes that don't hold still — they shift, rearranging, as if the stone itself is thinking.*
>
> *The air is different here. Heavier. Older. The spear pulses in long, slow throbs now, like a heart slowing toward sleep.*
>
> *Thusnelda kneels at the altar. She says: "Leave nothing at the door. What you carry in, you carry to the altar. All of it. The weapon, the doubts, and whatever part of you this journey has taken."*

**The four ritual requirements:**

1. Spear on the altar, unwrapped — bare iron on stone
2. Blood from a warrior — voluntary, 1d6 damage, cannot be healed until after the ritual
3. Group speaks in unison: *"We unmake what was made in darkness."* (Latin or Germanic — both work)
4. A sacrifice — willingly given, of genuine value

**Sacrifice table:**

| Offer | What it costs | Grove's response |
|---|---|---|
| A valuable magic item | Loss of power | Acceptable |
| A proficiency | Lose one skill proficiency permanently | Acceptable |
| A memory | One important memory — gone | Acceptable; grove returns a dream in its place |
| A year of life | Lifespan shortened | Acceptable |
| Cassia volunteers herself | Her death, willingly | More than acceptable — Thusnelda moves to stop her |
| Something worth less than the character cares about | Nothing real | The altar goes cold. The grove knows. |

*"That is not a sacrifice. That is a fee. The grove is not a toll booth."* — Thusnelda, immediately.

**The influenced NPC's crisis:**

As the ritual begins, the connection intensifies. The moment the spear touches the altar, they feel it most acutely.

- If detected and supported: group Wisdom check DC 14. Success: they participate, corruption cleared. Failure: they physically reach for the spear — Athletics grapple DC 12 to stop them, or someone calling their name three times. If stopped: they collapse, weeping, with no memory of the last hour.
- If undetected: they attempt to stop the ritual with increasingly urgent arguments. At the ritual's climax they try to take the spear and run.

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 5: Mars Intervenes</summary>

**Read aloud:**

> *"MORTALS."*
>
> *The word is not a sound. It moves through you like a wave, like a bell struck inside your chest.*
>
> *"YOU DARE UNMAKE WHAT A GOD FORGED."*
>
> *The standing stones crack. Not shattering — cracking, like old bones.*
>
> *Thusnelda doesn't move. Her voice is steady: "Finish the ritual. Do not look up. Whatever you see, do not look up."*

**Three paths forward (can be combined):**

**Option A — Defensive Hold:** 3 animated standing stones (Stone Golem stat blocks, 120 HP, CR 10 avatars — not killable at L5). Each party member fighting a golem occupies it for 2 rounds. Cover positions behind north/south stones displace golem movement by one round each. Golems fade when ritual completes.

**Option B — Skill Challenge (4 successes before 3 failures):**

| Check | DC | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Religion (active: speaking words of unmaking with genuine conviction) | 14 | Core ritual roll |
| Arcana (active: channeling the grove's power, not fighting it) | 15 | |
| Athletics (active: holding the spear steady as it fights back) | 12 | |
| Insight (active: resisting the spear's final promise) | 14 | *"They'll abandon you. Take me and they won't have to."* |
| Stealth (active: repositioning behind standing stones) | 13 | Defense, not ritual — on success, golem wastes one movement; ritual holder has advantage this round |

Each failure: one more animated stone joins.

**Option C — Bargain (before ritual begins):** Persuasion DC 17 or Religion DC 16, addressing Mars directly and naming what the spear did in his name:

> *"Great Mars, the spear was being used to corrupt and destroy men in your name. We destroy it not to defy you, but because what it was doing dishonored what you stand for."*

A long silence. Then: *"...CONTINUE. I WILL NOT MAKE IT EASY. BUT I WILL NOT STOP IT."*

Advantage on all Skill Challenge rolls.

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>📁 Conclusion + Session Handoff</summary>

**If the spear is destroyed:**

> *The iron shatters — not with a bang, but with a sound like an exhalation. Like something finally resting.*
>
> *The runes on the standing stones go dark. The air clears. Somewhere far away, in a direction that isn't quite north, you hear a sound that might be a god, furious, far off.*
>
> *The influenced NPC's eyes clear. They look at their hands. They say nothing for a long time.*
>
> *Thusnelda sweeps iron fragments into a clay pot and seals it with beeswax. "I will bury these in seven places. Go before he finds his voice again."*

Any corruption below level 5 is reduced by 1. Level 5 characters remain affected.

**Advance to Level 6.**

**Session 3 → Session 4 transition:**

| Question | Session 4 implication |
|---|---|
| Was the ritual successful? | Yes: party carries Thusnelda's sealed clay jar (spear fragments). No: party carries the whole spear. |
| Citizenship papers | Yes: Corvinus sends a clerk with draft commendationes forms. No: papers defer to Session 4 conclusion. |
| Cassia's bog valerian | Gathered: Siege Ward available in Session 4 (3 uses, 2d8 HP + clear 1 exhaustion). Not gathered: no ward. |
